ai.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
ai.brief: “SignDrop” exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights. Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. ” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates.

sec.title: Unpatched Check Point Gateways Are Being Wiped exploiting PHP2Shell
sec.brief: S. 7 million people Starting on 30 October, an attacker scanned and exploited Check Point Security Gateways that hadn’t been patched, going in through the Mobile Access portal. Check Point Research describes the activity as PHP2Shell for initial access, followed by a root-level privilege escalation tracked as CVE-2026-123039. ]204. ]204 targeted Israeli organizations through vulnerable Mobile Access portals on Check Point Security Gateways. ” reads the report . “Following initial access, the attacker escalated privileges from the portal service account to root by exploiting CVE-2026-123039 , a local privilege-escalation vulnerability in the DynamicCLI IPC interface. ”
